notes: Power is a real operating cost now. Routers, caches, optical gear and servers draw power, cooling adds 35%, and each city has its own tariff. Check the Power & cooling section in Infra or compare POPs in the NOC.

UPS batteries bridge one game day, generators burn diesel while the grid is down, and an independent second feed protects against local faults. Regional blackouts can take both feeds down. Batteries must recharge.

Maintenance happens automatically. The NOC gives seven days' notice; redundant routers are serviced and swapped one at a time without customer impact. A single router goes down for a day. Generator and server service is automatic too, and optical channels periodically need maintenance.
A full NOC event log remembers the latest 300 entries, including recovery, maintenance and customer changes. Filter by category or search by city.

Open server rooms: buy 20U racks, rent units to colocation tenants, or install your own web, cloud and DDoS scrubbing servers. New customers arrive weekly when service is healthy. Hosting brings traffic, power bills, operating costs, revenue and satisfaction; poor service causes churn.

Scrubbing is capacity-limited and depends on power and a live backbone path. Existing centers remain 400G appliances; extra servers add 100G each, limited by the POP's forwarding capacity. Attacks above capacity still hurt.
Existing saves get sensible defaults and a fresh maintenance schedule.
